newsitem.title: USA: States back Cincinnati campaign spending limit law.
newsitem.headline: States back Cincinnati campaign spending limit law.

text.p: A group of 25 state attorneys general asked an appeals court Tuesday to overturn a ruling that blocked spending limits on city council races here.
The case, Kruse vs Cincinnati, could ultimately be used to challenge a 1976 U.S. Supreme Court ruling that campaign spending limits violated the First Amendment right to free speech.

The attorneys general filed a "friend of the court" brief in the U.S. 6th Circuit Court of Appeals, backing the city's appeal for a reversal of U.S. District Judge Herman Weber's January ruling that the ordinance, limiting spending on city council races to $140,000, was unconstitutional.
A spokesman for Ohio Attorney General Betty Montgomery said she and the other attorneys general believe each state should be allowed to regulate its election system by enacting spending limits.

John Bonifaz of the National Voting Rights Institute, who was representing Cincinnati in the appeal, said he hoped the case would reach the U.S. Supreme Court and induce the justices to re-examine their 1976 decision in the case blocking spending limits.
John Kruse, an unsuccessful Republican candidate for Cincinnati City Council in 1995, used that high court decision as the basis for his challenge of the Cincinnati ordinance.
